results.title: DGX Spark price: $6,950 US, €7,332 in Europe (October 2026) | GPUwerk
results.author: Samuel Seidel
highlights:
# DGX Spark price

By Samuel Seidel · Published September 14, 2026 · Updated 24 October 2026 · 7 min read

The 128 GB DGX Spark costs $6,950 in the US on NVIDIA's own marketplace (checked 11 October 2026, listed out of stock), up from $4,699 in February and $3,999 at launch. In Europe the cheapest Founders Edition offer in Germany was €7,331.59 including VAT on 24 October 2026. A 64 GB model went on sale through NVIDIA's partners on 23 October 2026, starting at $4,999. To rent instead, a dedicated 128 GB Spark is $0.79 per hour billed per minute, and a two-node cluster is $1.79 per hour.

...

| What | Price | Where | Checked |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| DGX Spark 128 GB, US list | $6,950 | NVIDIA marketplace | 11 October 2026 |
| DGX Spark 64 GB, US | From $4,999 | Partners only, per the NVIDIA blog, 2 October 2026 | 24 October 2026 |
| DGX Spark 128 GB, Germany | From €7,331.59 incl. VAT | Cheapest of 21 shop offers on geizhals.de | 24 October 2026 |
| Lenovo ThinkStation PGX 128 GB, 1 TB (same GB10 chip) | €4,666 excl. VAT | Bechtle Belgium | 24 October 2026 |
| Rent a 128 GB Spark | $0.79 per hour | GPUwerk, billed per minute | 24 October 2026 |

What I verified and what I did not. On 11 October 2026 the NVIDIA marketplace listing showed $6,950 for the 128 GB DGX Spark, marked out of stock. On 24 October 2026 that page did not load for me, so the $6,950 figure is from 11 October. The NVIDIA product page, read 24 October 2026, shows no price and says the 64 GB configuration is available only through participating OEM partners. The 64 GB price and on-sale date are from the NVIDIA blog, 2 October 2026. I could not find a partner listing that showed the 64 GB model in stock on 24 October.

## Price history

The US list price of the 128 GB machine has risen twice in a year. NVIDIA gave memory supply as the reason in February, and The Register gives memory prices as the reason in October.

| Date | Price | Event | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 15 October 2025 | $3,999 (128 GB) | Orders open on NVIDIA.com and at partners | NVIDIA newsroom, 13 Oct 2025; $3,999 confirmed as the prior price in the February forum post |
| 23 February 2026 | $4,699 (128 GB) | Increase of $700, worldwide, blamed on memory supply constraints; no hardware change | NVIDIA forum announcement |
| 2 October 2026 | $6,950 (128 GB) | Increase reported the same day NVIDIA announced the 64 GB model | NVIDIA marketplace, $6,950 on 11 Oct 2026; The Register, 2 Oct 2026 for the date |
| 23 October 2026 | From $4,999 (64 GB) | 64 GB model on sale through Acer, ASUS, Dell, Gigabyte, HP and MSI | NVIDIA blog, 2 October 2026 |

Checked 2026-10-11 and 2026-10-24. The forum post is titled 23 February 2026, is dated 25 February, and says the price applies to all regions. Retailers can lag: the forum post says other sales channels may take longer to reflect a change. Why memory-heavy hardware got more expensive through 2026 is covered in the 2026 GPU memory shortage.

...

NVIDIA's blog of 2 October 2026 gives the 64 GB model a start price of $4,999 and an on-sale date of 23 October 2026, through Acer, ASUS, Dell, Gigabyte, HP and MSI. NVIDIA does not sell it in its own store. The chip, networking and software are the same as on the 128 GB machine. The difference is memory. The 64 GB vs 128 GB guide has OEM prices and a fit table for current models.

...

GPUwerk and the 64 GB model: GPUwerk rents only 128 GB machines. It does not rent out 64 GB units and does not accept them for hosting or for its rent-out programme.

...

| Lenovo ThinkStation PGX | 2 TB | EUR 5,890 | EUR 7,126.90 at 21% Czech VAT | GPUwerk store | On sale, delivery date to be confirmed; excludes shipping | 2026-10-24 |
| Lenovo ThinkStation PGX | 4 TB | EUR 6,280 | EUR 7,598.80 at 21% Czech VAT | GPUwerk store | On sale, delivery date to be confirmed; excludes shipping | 2026-10-24 |
| NVIDIA DGX Spark | 4 TB | No fixed price | No fixed price | GPUwerk store | Priced from Czech suppliers' stock; orderable only when a supplier can deliver | 2026-10-24 |

...

US partner prices were already above NVIDIA's list before October. In the NVIDIA forum thread September 2026 availability of GB10s, a user reported on 2 September 2026 that the ASUS eShop listed the Ascent GX10 at $6,000, $7,000 and $8,000 for 1 TB, 2 TB and 4 TB, while NVIDIA's Founders Edition was $4,699.

...

## Rent instead

When you rent a DGX Spark on GPUwerk, a dedicated machine is $0.79 per hour, billed per minute against prepaid credit, in USD excluding tax, with 1 TB NVMe and no egress fees. The cluster of two linked nodes is $1.79 per hour. A stopped instance holds its machine at 75% of the running rate.

| Usage | Cost |
| --- | --- |
| 1 hour | $0.79 |
| 8 hours | $6.32 |
| 24 hours | $18.96 |
| 730 hours (a month, always on) | $576.70 |
| Reserved, 12 months (25% off) | $432.53 per month, about $0.59 per hour |

At the $6,950 list price (checked 11 October 2026), a Spark that runs around the clock reaches the purchase price after about 8,800 hours at the on-demand rate, roughly 12 months, before electricity, VAT and resale value. Owning wins past that point, and renting wins below it. The rent-vs-buy page has a calculator, and the pricing page has the reserved terms. If you want to own one without running it yourself, the store sells the PGX with hosting at GPUwerk as an optional add-on; any rental income from a hosted machine depends on demand and is not guaranteed.

...

The 128 GB DGX Spark is $6,950 in the US on NVIDIA's own marketplace, checked 11 October 2026 (listed out of stock). It launched at $3,999 and went to $4,699 on 23 February 2026. In Germany the cheapest Founders Edition offer on geizhals.de was €7,331.59 including VAT on 24 October 2026. The 64 GB model starts at $4,999 through NVIDIA's partners, on sale since 23 October 2026. Renting a dedicated Spark from GPUwerk is $0.79 per hour, billed per minute.

Why did the DGX Spark price go up?

NVIDIA attributed the February 2026 increase from $3,999 to $4,699 to industry-wide memory supply constraints, in its forum announcement. The Register attributes the October 2026 increase to $6,950 to rising memory prices as well. I have not found an NVIDIA statement for the October change.

results.title: Rent a DGX Spark: $0.79/h billed by the minute, six steps to SSH
results.author: Samuel Seidel
highlights:
# How to rent a DGX Spark

By Samuel Seidel · Published September 14, 2026 · Updated October 24, 2026 · 8 min read

A DGX Spark rents for $0.79/hour, billed per minute from prepaid credit, and your first $20 top-up comes with $30 in credit. Sign in, top up, deploy, then open the browser terminal, which needs no SSH key, or connect as root over SSH with your own key. The six steps below follow the console in order.

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Hardware | DGX Spark GB10 (ARM64), 128 GB unified memory, 1 TB NVMe shared with the system and model cache |
| Price | $0.79/hour, billed per minute, prepaid, excluding VAT per the terms. A two-node cluster is $1.79/hour. See pricing. |
| First top-up | Pay $20, get $30 in credit. The minimum top-up is $20. |
| Location | Europe (EEA) by default: GPUwerk's own Sparks in Czechia and partner Sparks in other EEA countries. Partner Sparks in the US and Hong Kong only if you choose them; see locations and Partner Sparks below. Details: GDPR and the EU AI Act on dedicated hardware. |
| Tenancy | Dedicated, one tenant per machine |
| Access | Browser terminal, or root SSH to your own container (root inside it, not on the host). CUDA 13.0 toolkit preinstalled. systemd and Docker inside the rental on some machines only; the others run a plain container without them, and you can't choose which (details). |
| Stopping | Held at 75% of the rate, $0.59/hour, with your workspace kept. Terminate deletes the workspace. |
| Other providers | Other DGX Spark rental offers are listed, with sources, on the cloud providers page. |

Checked against GPUwerk's pricing page and terms on October 24, 2026.

## How much does it cost to rent a DGX Spark?

One DGX Spark costs $0.79 an hour, billed per minute, so a minute costs about 1.3 cents. Prices exclude VAT. Here is what that comes to if the Spark runs the whole time:

| Running time | Cost at $0.79/h |
| --- | --- |
| 1 hour | $0.79 |
| 8 hours | $6.32 |
| 1 day (24 hours) | $18.96 |
| 1 week (168 hours) | $132.72 |
| 20 hours a month | $15.80 a month |
| 80 hours a month | $63.20 a month |
| 160 hours a month | $126.40 a month |
| Always on (730 hours) | $576.70 a month, or less on a monthly reservation |

A stopped Spark is billed at 75% of the rate, $0.59 an hour, so terminate it when you no longer need the workspace. A two-node cluster is $1.79 an hour. All rates are on the pricing page.

Vast.ai is a marketplace of 68+ GPU types where each host sets the price, billed per second; GPUwerk rents one machine, a dedicated NVIDIA DGX Spark with 128 GB of unified memory in EU-Central, for a flat $0.79/hour billed per minute. Vast.ai's own GB10 page listed no DGX Spark offers on 9 November 2026, so if a Spark is the machine you want, that is the gap GPUwerk fills. results.title: Scaling from one DGX Spark to a fleet | GPUwerk
results.author: Samuel Seidel
highlights: Each additional Spark is a separate deploy in the console, billed by the minute at the same $0.79/hour on-demand rate as the first. There is no published fleet discount (monthly reservations of 1 to 24 months carry term discounts per node; see pricing), and no shared billing entity across instances: each is its own instance with its own hostname, its own workspace, and its own bill. Check availability in the console before assuming a second node is free, the way you would for the first.

results.title: Cold start vs always-on: choosing an instance uptime pattern | GPUwerk
results.author: Samuel Seidel
highlights:
## What each state actually costs and keeps

Per the pricing page, a running Spark bills the full $0.79/hour on-demand rate. Stopping an instance keeps it held for you (the same machine, the same SSH port and hostname, workspace intact) at 75% of the running rate: $0.59/hour. Terminating ends billing entirely, but it also deletes the workspace for good, with no copy kept. That's why the console asks you to type the instance name to confirm.
